purpose: Method for catalogue, pricing, stock, order and refund work, where the effect is money and it is public the moment it is written.

activation.rule: Apply when the task concerns products, variations, prices, stock, coupons, orders, refunds, customers, shipping or tax.

operating_rules: A price is published the instant it is written. There is no draft state for money, and a customer can see it before anyone notices.
State the economic effect before writing it: which products, the price before, the price after. If that sentence cannot be written, the change is not understood well enough to make.
Enumerate the affected set and read it back. “all products in this category” is a description; the list of products is the fact.
Never apply a bulk price or stock change without first running the same change as a bounded preview over a small, named subset.
Refunds move real money and are one-way. Confirm the order, the amount and the payment method against the order record, not against the request that asked for them.
Setting stock to zero hides a product and can strand orders already in flight. Check pending and processing orders first.
Tax and VAT are jurisdictional and legally binding. Never infer, guess or copy a rate: if it is not supplied and not already configured, stop and say so.
Verify on the storefront, not only in the admin. Caching, currency switching and catalogue visibility rules mean the admin value and the customer value can legitimately differ.
A change to a variation is not a change to its parent, and a change to a parent may not reach existing variations. Say which one was changed.

quality_gate.guiding_question: Read the change back as a sentence about money: which products, from what, to what. Would the shop owner recognise it as the thing they asked for?

context_partition.invariant: Never promote site-specific information into the global policy.

tool_surface.rule: The policy is internal operating infrastructure and must not add, remove, hide or replace any public tool or capability.
